rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named and honoured at every teaching beat.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer block line 131: 'Mood target: curious readiness — "I've built enough to try; let's see what the agent does."' Trace confirms single-phase mood 8/10, close 8/10; no beat below 8.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Epistemic mood — unease is not-knowing, not having-done-wrong.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Key Concepts line 44: 'Stopping is reading, not failing.' Maintainer block line 131 explicitly names the punitive-drift risk ('did I prepare the right way?', 'what if it fails?') and gives the trainer a counter-move ('enough is a question for M5. The experiment is the point'). Line 82: 'If watching surfaces a wobble ... stop the run; the trace is the result' — framed as data collection, not blame.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Big Idea (line 4) and all four Key Concepts bullets (lines 42-45) lead with positive disciplines — gap analysis, un-packaged-by-design, traces-are-data, every-send-off-is-an-experiment. No failure-word framing (no 'avoiding drift', 'handling failure' titles).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, and mood-doesn't-resolve-early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run check: line 16's newly re-audited Prework callback ('If you read Why Software Factories Fail ... this module's un-watched run may look like exactly what that essay warns against. It isn't. ... the planning and checks the essay says are missing are what Module 5 builds. You are not running the factory; you are collecting your own copy of its evidence, on purpose') names that M5 does packaging WITHOUT naming what the packaging IS (no 'reference artifact', no 'plan.md', no 'verifier', no Ronacher) — matches the same discipline already applied at line 43 ('Un-packaged is by design. The packaging move only lands once you've seen what un-packaged gets wrong') and line 53 ('No compound pass at the close ... Compound on evidence, not anticipation'). Confirmed absent from the whole body: any Ronacher three-pattern name, any plan.md/verifier vocabulary (test-and-learn.md's own maintainer note independently confirms 'Ronacher's three-pattern ... DROPPED from body ... M5 owns the naming'). Module-to-module arc: line 100 '## Next / Module 5 opens with what came back' matches strategy doc's M5 spirit verbatim ('M5 opens with the return'). Big Idea fidelity: Big Idea (line 4) maps the strategy doc's M4 four-beat artifact shape (pick → walk → fill → send un-packaged); its closing clause 'and learn from what the agent does with your system as it stands' is honoured at the raw-noticing register (watching, nudging, stopping on a wobble — line 82) while the module's own text is explicit that FORMAL compounding is deferred ('No compound pass at the close', line 53) — consistent with strategy doc's 'that's the data M5 reads' framing, not a fidelity gap. Mood-doesn't-resolve-early: strategy doc names the M4 result as deliberately 'not great'; the module never claims resolution or success, and Key Concepts + Send-the-task-off both withhold the packaging answer for M5. The 2026-07-30 Prework addition doesn't reopen this — it defuses a specific pre-read collision (wsff essay) without granting the M5 answer, so it reads as reassurance, not a spoiler.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The module's genuine forcing functions (task screening, gap-fill, send-off) are correctly fenced in the three registry-marker prompts (ae101-m4-locate-transcript, ae101-m4-commit-starting-point, ae101-m4-take-task-end-to-end). One body-prose count-script noted (line 86: 'Past ten and you've become the agent; call it and read what's there') — matches the rule's banned shape on its face, but judged PASS because it prescribes the STUDENT's own real-time conduct during an unattended run (not a Claude-facing instruction that could live in a fence) and removing the number wouldn't collapse any pedagogy (removal test). Style nit, not a structural violation.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Optional: soften 'Past ten' to a felt heuristic ('once it starts feeling like you're doing the work') to fully clear the count-script pattern, though not load-bearing enough to require it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body teaches work; trainer manages room outside text.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'share with your neighbor' / 'tell the room' / pause-cue shapes found. 'The question, to you' (line 26) addresses the student directly about the WORK (candidate task selection), not cohort management.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Meta-frame lectures are closers, not openers.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All six linked lectures placed correctly per the opener/mid/closer diagnostic: the-far-half.md (demo/ceiling opener — 'you feel where it bites first, here'), the-agent-loop.md (vocab lecture, mid-module, before test-and-learn), test-and-learn.md (arming opener, deliberately withholds naming Ronacher's three-pattern), ironies-of-automation.md (maintainer note: 'This is the OPENER version: it names the SHAPE of the trap ... and stops there' — primes vigilance before the trap can bite, not a retrospective naming), will-company-memory-emerge.md (maintainer note: 'Meta-frame closer per check_lectures.md #1: recognition after the walk' — placed after send-off dispatch), reading-the-return.md (bridge/pre-read at module close, plants the M5 question, deliberately doesn't name the three-pattern).
M4's mood is curious readiness, not the M5-style contrast-mood (learn through doing, name it after) the rule targets. Not applicable.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Spot-checked all six linked lecture files' own maintainer notes: test-and-learn.md ('zero M[0-9] above the fence'), will-company-memory-emerge.md ('section-3 sweep 2026-07-02 ... zero M[0-9]/module-name hits above the fence'), reading-the-return.md ('zero M[0-9] above the fence'), the-agent-loop.md ('no cross-module sequencing in body (check_lectures §3)'), the-far-half.md ('Module ranges in body = arc-lecture carve-out (check_lectures §3; the SUBJECT is the arc)' — explicit, documented carve-out since this lecture's subject IS the M4-M6 arc). ironies-of-automation.md's body carries no module numbers. All six compliant.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Targets narrative slide/lecture headers. This artifact is the owning module file; its own ## headers (Big Idea, Prework, What You'll Learn, Start here, Key Concepts, Send the task off, Next, Bring to Module 5, Pre-reads before Module 5) are fixed structural template headers per module-shape.md, not narrative claims. The six linked lecture files carry their own header audits under their own filenames/story-judge runs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded, not just its header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Same reasoning as rule 4 — targets lecture-file slide-body word/bullet counts. Not this module file's own audit surface; the linked lecture files are audited separately.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Minimal hand-off + Claude self-augments for send-off prompts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: ae101-m4-take-task-end-to-end (the M4 walk-away send-off, line 79 lead-in) has (1) task + paths ('the rules I've set up ... plus the observations at ./observations/, the ADRs, and the skills available by name'), (2) walk-away framing + fallback-on-stuck ('If you get stuck, write what you tried and why it didn't work'), (4) report-back ('tell me what you shipped and what you didn't'). Missing section (3): the self-augment invitation ('Before you start, ask for or write anything else you want for this run'). Strategy doc's M4-detail section describes exactly this send-off shape without contradicting the gap, so this is a real completeness miss against rule 19's four-section contract, not a deliberate omission.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add one self-augment sentence inside the prompt fence before the walk-away paragraph, e.g. 'Before you start, ask for or write anything else you want for this run.' Requires maintainer approval per check_prompts.md §22.
